Create Grouped Cross-Validation Folds

Source: R/cv_folds.R
grouped_cv_folds.Rd

Keep all rows from a sampling group in the same assessment fold, so that a held-out row is never predicted with help from its own group. Whole groups are assigned to folds to balance the row counts, largest groups first.

Usage

grouped_cv_folds(group, k = 5, ids = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'multiScaleR_folds'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

group

Vector of sampling-group labels, one per row, such as site, animal, year, or choice-set IDs. Missing or empty labels are rejected.

k

Number of folds, at least two and no greater than the number of groups. The default is five.

ids

Unique character row IDs, in the order of group. Use the row names of the modeling data. The default uses the names of group, or the row numbers as character strings when group is unnamed. Named groups must align exactly with supplied IDs.

x

A multiScaleR_folds object, for print().

...

Not used. Reserved for future print controls.

Value

A named list of class multiScaleR_folds with one element per fold (fold1, fold2, and so on), ready for cross_validate() and the other cross-validation functions. Each element holds two character vectors of row IDs, analysis (rows used to fit) and assessment (rows held out). Every row is assessed exactly once. The attribute fold_info holds the method ("grouped"), k, an assignment data frame with the row_id, group, unit, and assessment fold of every row, and excluded, the IDs left out of each fold's training rows (none for grouped folds). print() shows the number of analysis, assessment, and excluded rows in each fold, and returns x invisibly.

Details

Assignment is deterministic and does not use the random-number generator, so the same call always gives the same folds. Groups of equal size are ordered by their labels. Balancing row counts does not stratify the responses. Choose the sampling groups and the prediction question before you look at any scores. To keep groups together within spatial blocks, pass them as group to spatial_cv_folds(). Building folds does not decide which models can be scored. For matched choice sets, score the folds with cross_validate_clogit(). vignette("v08-cross-validation", package = "multiScaleR") compares grouped, spatial, and random fold designs.

See also

spatial_cv_folds(), cross_validate(), cv_tab()

Examples

# Twelve records from six sites, two visits each
ids <- paste0("row", 1:12)
folds <- grouped_cv_folds(rep(letters[1:6], each = 2), k = 3, ids = ids)
folds                    # rows fitted and held out in each fold
#> Cross-validation folds: grouped 
#>   fold analysis assessment excluded
#>  fold1        8          4        0
#>  fold2        8          4        0
#>  fold3        8          4        0
folds$fold1$assessment   # both visits to a site are held out together
#> [1] "row1" "row2" "row7" "row8"
